summary:
The Durango Shiner once glimmered in the quiet waters of the Rio del Tunal, a single reservoir nestled within the upper Rio Mezquital drainage basin of Durango, Mexico. This small freshwater fish, known to science from only two collections, occupied one of the most confined ranges of any species — a narrow stretch of water that was, for a time, entirely its world.

As Durango City grew through the mid-twentieth century, the Rio del Tunal could not withstand the pressure. Pollution, reduced streamflow, and the introduction of predatory species like largemouth bass reshaped the river beyond recognition. The Durango Shiner was last seen in 1961. Decades of searching have found nothing. It is gone.
